verdict.rationale: Runpod documents a REST API v1 that gives "programmatic access to all Runpod compute resources," plus a GraphQL API with cURL examples for Pod lifecycle and Serverless SDKs for Python, JavaScript and Go. A runtime probe confirmed the REST API serves its OpenAPI spec and is live and API-key-gated as documented. Missing for 10: no hands-on evidence of a full authenticated workflow (e.g. creating and terminating a Pod) run end-to-end through the API; the probe only confirms the spec and the auth gate.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The Runpod REST API v1 provides programmatic access to all Runpod compute resources. Integrate GPU infrastructure into your applications, workflows, and automation systems.
Use the GraphQL API to manage Pods, templates, and Serverless endpoints through queries and mutations.
Create, start, stop, and query Pods using the GraphQL API with cURL and GraphQL examples.
Install and configure the Serverless SDK for Python, JavaScript, or Go to interact with Serverless endpoints programmatically.

https://rest.runpod.io/v1/openapi.json serves the REST API's OpenAPI spec keylessly, and a bare GET to https://rest.runpod.io/v1/pods answers HTTP 401 — the Pod-provisioning REST API is live and API-key-gated exactly as documented.
